title: Say hello and thank you
goal: At any shop or café, greet the person in Turkish and thank them when you leave. No English at all for these two moments.
tips: Smile and say it first — people in Cyprus love it when foreigners try.

title: Greet a shopkeeper and say thank you
goal: Greet a shopkeeper, buy one thing, say thank you and goodbye — all in Turkish.
tips: 'Kolay gelsin' is what locals say to anyone working — it always gets a warm reaction.

title: Introduce yourself
goal: Tell a neighbour or colleague your name, where you're from and that you're learning Turkish.
tips: Swap in your own country: -li / -lı / -lu / -lü + -yim (Amerikalıyım, Almanyalıyım).

title: Order a coffee fully in Turkish
goal: Order a Turkish coffee with your sugar preference and pay — fully in Turkish.
place: A café in Lefkoşa or Girne
tips: Sade = no sugar, az şekerli = a little, orta = medium, şekerli = sweet.

title: Buy bread at the bakery
goal: Ask for a specific number of items at a bakery (e.g. 'iki tane pilavuna').
tips: 'Tane' is the counter word — use it with numbers when buying pieces.

title: Ask for directions
goal: Ask a passer-by where a place is, and understand at least 'sağ', 'sol' or 'düz'.

phrases.en: Excuse me, where is the pharmacy?
On the right or the left?

tips: Ask about somewhere you already know — then you can check your understanding.

title: Take a dolmuş
goal: Ask the driver if the dolmuş goes to your destination and ask to get off.
place: A dolmuş in Lefkoşa or to Girne

phrases.en: Can I get off somewhere convenient?

tips: 'Müsait bir yerde' is the standard way to ask a driver to stop.

title: Ask the price at the market
goal: Ask the price of three different things and buy one of them by the kilo.
place: The Wednesday market (Lefkoşa) or any pazar
tips: Prepare your numbers before you go: kırk, elli, altmış, yüz.

title: Eat at a lokanta
goal: Order a main dish and a drink, ask for the bill — in Turkish.
tips: In a lokanta you can point at the dishes — 'bundan' (of this) is your friend.

title: Buy fruit by weight
goal: Buy two kinds of fruit, specifying weight or number, and ask if they are fresh.

phrases.en: Half a kilo of cherries, please.

tips: Use what's in season — Güzelyurt oranges in winter, karpuz in summer.

title: Weather small talk
goal: Start a 3-line conversation about the weather with a colleague or neighbour.

phrases.tr: Bugün hava çok sıcak, değil mi?
phrases.en: It's very hot today, isn't it?
What's the weather like here in winter?

tips: 'değil mi?' turns any statement into 'isn't it?' — very useful.

title: Ask a colleague about their weekend
goal: Ask a colleague 3 questions about their weekend and react to the answers.
tips: You'll hear past tense (-dı/-di) — listen for gittim, yaptım, gezdim.

title: Make an appointment
goal: Book an appointment (barber, hairdresser, doctor) in Turkish, including a day and time.

phrases.en: I'd like to make an appointment.

tips: Write the days and times you can do on paper first.

title: Describe your daily routine
goal: Tell someone 4 things you do every day (present tense).

phrases.en: I get up at six every morning.
I go to work by bus.
In the afternoon I write my thesis.
In the evening I study Turkish.

tips: Practise saying it aloud in the morning while making coffee.

title: Tell what you did yesterday
goal: Tell a colleague 3 things you did yesterday (past tense).

phrases.en: I had a meal with my friend.
In the evening I watched a film.

tips: Fıstıkçı şahap: after p, ç, t, k, s, ş, h, f the past is -tı/-ti: gittim, yaptım.

title: Ask for help at the pharmacy
goal: Describe a small symptom and ask for something for it.

phrases.tr: Bunun için bir şey var mı?

tips: Even if you're well, you can ask about sunscreen: 'Güneş kremi var mı?'

title: Make weekend plans
goal: Invite someone to do something this weekend and agree a time and place (future tense).

phrases.en: What will you do on Saturday?

tips: -acağım / -eceğim: remember k → ğ before a vowel.

title: Describe your home
goal: Describe where you live: neighbourhood, rooms, what you like.
tips: Possessive + var = 'I have': balkonum var, bahçemiz var.

title: Ask for another size or colour
goal: In a clothes or shoe shop, ask for a different size or colour.
tips: Colour + -(s)I = 'the X one': mavisi, siyahı, kırmızısı.

title: Recommend a place
goal: Recommend one place in Northern Cyprus to someone and say what they can do there.
place: Talking to a visitor or colleague
tips: -(y)Abil = can: gidebilirsin, görebilirsin, yiyebilirsin.

title: Ask permission politely
goal: Use '-abilir miyim?' three times this week in real situations.
tips: This is the most useful polite structure in Turkish — use it everywhere.

title: Explain your research
goal: Explain your PhD topic in 3 simple Turkish sentences to a Turkish-speaking colleague.

phrases.en: The topic of my PhD is …

tips: Prepare the sentences in the Write tab first and get them corrected.

title: Report a problem
goal: Tell your landlord, a repairman or reception that something is broken, and ask when it can be fixed.
tips: bozuldu = broke down (past). Combine with 'Ne zaman …?'.

title: A 10-minute conversation
goal: Have a 10-minute conversation in Turkish with a neighbour, colleague or shopkeeper. Switch to English only if completely stuck.
tips: Ask questions — then the other person does most of the talking.
